verdicts.threatModel: Attacker would need to tamper with the GeoNames dump (compromise download.geonames.org or break TLS) to feed altered place-name data to `metadata.downloadPlaceNames`; there is no local attacker-controlled source.
verdicts.reachability: Reachable: engine/src/cmd/geocode.rs:176-177 calls `download_url` with `FileSpec{sha256: None}` on `GEONAMES_BASE` (https); `base_allowed` (geocode.rs:213) forces https or loopback http. The payload is a zip of tab-separated text, read with MAX_ZIP 64 MiB, extracted with MAX_TEXT, and parsed into bounded place records (MAX_PLACES, MAX_NAME); it is never executed or loaded as code.
verdicts.impact: Low. A tampered dump could only yield wrong or junk place names offered for photo location metadata; caps and the never-crash parser bound availability effects. It is a data file, not a binary, and GeoNames republishes the dump daily, so a fixed digest cannot be pinned.
verdicts.rationale: Scanner rule targets unpinned binaries; this is a TLS-fetched, size-capped, parsed-only text dataset from a rolling upstream. Devil's advocate: an integrity pin is absent, but with no code execution and mutable upstream it is not a vulnerability; at most a data-integrity hardening idea.
